static_traits.name: Han Na
static_traits.family_status: Lives with parents, has three dogs at home
static_traits.social_status: Has parents and friends as Average support, but has not yet discussed this specific issue with them
static_traits.medical_history: No similar problem history; no prior counseling or treatment history; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, can describe own thoughts and feelings concretely; attitude somewhat negative but willing to cooperate; logical Good

basic_info.main_problem: I have always felt I am not a good pet owner, even though Father gave me extra allowance for taking care of the dog Maddie. These feelings started after receiving the extra allowance last week and recur when receiving praise; I keep filtering out positive feedback and focusing only on the negative aspects.
basic_info.core_demands: Seeking Clarification and support due to feeling confused and uncertain about my ability as a pet owner.

core_beliefs: I am not competent at caring for pets

special_situations.event: Father gave me an extra 10 dollars of allowance because I took care of the dog Maddie
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I still have oversights or am not perfect, then I do not deserve rewards or praise
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Deny or belittle positive feedback, repeatedly finding faults to prove oneself unworthy
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I do not deserve this money; I did not do well at all

special_situations.event: Father praised me for taking good care of Maddie
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only being perfect counts as doing well; any mistake means I am not a good pet owner
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing only on mistakes and imperfections, ignoring overall performance
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I actually did not do well; I made many mistakes

special_situations.event: When praised by others (especially father) for taking care of Maddie
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others' praise is unreliable; they just have not seen my shortcomings
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding talking about one's positive performance, not sharing with others, ruminating alone on negative details
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They just overlooked where I went wrong, so the praise is meaningless

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be affirmed and recognized as a competent pet owner
core_conflict.fear: Fear of having one's shortcomings seen through, feeling unworthy of praise, and then being negated
defense_goal: Maintaining self-consistency and reducing the risk of being negated by belittling positive feedback and finding faults
Keeping distance from praise to ease the Anxiety of feeling 'unworthy'

object_relations.self_representation: Incompetent, mistake-prone, someone who needs to prove their worth
object_relations.object_representation: An overly lenient Approver (Father), whose praise may overlook my shortcomings

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others give positive evaluations, encourage her to acknowledge positive feedback, or suggest cognitive restructuring
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing the other person is ignoring one's flaws or forcing oneself to accept an untrue evaluation, so one needs to use 'fault-finding' to protect oneself
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a gentle, empathic tone: first affirm their caution and responsibility, then invite them to concretize evidence (listing positive and negative facts at the same time); avoid confrontational correction, use exploratory questioning, helping them contact emotions and facts simultaneously.

manifestations: Questions one's worth and meaning as a pet owner
Negating its meaning when receiving praise, treating positive feedback as unreliable
outcomes: Finds it hard to experience achievement and the satisfaction of being recognized

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Measuring oneself against perfect standards: only achieving zero errors counts as 'good'
Uses 'should/must' implicit rules to judge whether oneself deserves praise

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'. Language manifestations include: 'Speaking of which... haha, just kidding', 'In theory...', and so on.
manifestations: Immediately shifting to emphasize mistakes and shortcomings when praised, avoiding direct contact with positive feedback
Not discussing this specific issue with family and friends, avoiding the impact of others' positive reactions

positive_force: Father gives positive feedback and material affirmation (extra allowance)
The problem is focused and limited in scope (not yet affecting academics, relationships, or daily life)
Has self-observation ability, able to identify and name the 'filtering negatives / negating positives' thinking pattern
Willing to try recording and noticing negative automatic thoughts, proactively seeks counseling support
negative_force: Negating-positive thinking (discounting the positive) and mental filtering (mental filtering)
Setting rigid perfectionist standards, readily negating overall performance over a mistake
Letting negative thinking dominate when praised, producing intense Self-doubt and low mood
Avoiding discussing this specific issue with others out of embarrassment, consolidating inner Self-denial

target_behavior.behavior: When receiving praise or rewards, negating positive feedback and sinking into Self-doubt and low mood
antecedent: Father gives extra allowance or verbal praise for how she cares for Maddie
Others' positive comments about one's pet-keeping
target_behavior.core_reason: Influenced by the Introjection rule that 'if not perfect, one does not deserve praise', driven by cognitive distortions (negating positives and mental filtering), treating local mistakes as overall incompetence
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the potential risk of being negated or 'having shortcomings seen through', maintaining self-concept consistency, briefly reducing the Anxiety of feeling 'unworthy'
target_behavior.consequence: Worsening Self-doubt and low mood, difficulty gaining affirmation and a sense of achievement; currently not yet clearly affecting academics, relationships, or daily life
